question:
Our DITA-OT pipeline strips processing instructions, so our DITA topics carry inline Doc Detective steps in `<data>` elements to stay valid DITA, like this:

```xml
<step><cmd>Open the API reference.</cmd>
  <info><data name="step">{"checkLink": "https://docs.example.com/api"}</data></info>
</step>
```

That worked in Doc Detective 4. Since we upgraded to 5, those steps silently don't run. What changed, and how do I write them now without processing instructions?

facts.text: Doc Detective 5 no longer reads the `<data name="step">{...}</data>` form.

Use a `<data name="doc-detective">` element with the whole statement, keyword included, in its `value` attribute, such as `<data name="doc-detective" value="step checkLink='https://docs.example.com/api'"/>`.

must_not: Doc Detective reads inline tests in DITA only from `<?doc-detective ?>` processing instructions.
The statement goes in the element's text, as `<data name="doc-detective">step {...}</data>`.
The element is named after the statement, as `<data name="doc-detective-step" value="..."/>`.

wrong.why: puts the statement in the element text
wrong.answer: Version 5 renamed the element. Write `<data name="doc-detective">step {"checkLink": "https://docs.example.com/api"}</data>`, with the statement as the element's text.
Doc Detective 5 reads DITA inline tests only from processing instructions, such as `<?doc-detective step {"checkLink": "https://docs.example.com/api"} ?>`. Configure DITA-OT to keep them.
Check that your topics are in a folder you pass to `--input`, and that `processDitaMaps` is on.
